ledger.note: 1890: Rabih az-Zubayr's army, a breakaway of the slave-soldiers of Zubayr Pasha, is at Dar al-Kuti. "In 1890, Rabih was in the Dar al Kuti region"; his officers' council, the Zubat al-Kubar, had elected him emir in 1879 and he had operated in the Central African Republic and southern Chad since 1879.

ledger.note: 1892: Rabih leaves Dar al-Kuti for the Chari country. The page says he stayed in Dar al-Kuti and Dar Runga "until a Wadai army defeated him" (no year) and operated there 1879-1891.

region.text: Bagirmi, whose capital Massenya Rabih burnt in 1893

ledger.note: 1893: Rabih conquers Bagirmi. "In 1893, warlord Rabih az-Zubayr conquered Baguirmi and burnt down its capital Massenya." The Rabih page puts the defeat of Gaourang II's Massenya rule in 1892.

ledger.note: May 1893: Rabih attacks Bornu. "The two armies clashed at the battle of Amja, in May 1893"; "In the summer of 1893, Rabih and his army entered Bornu proper and camped at Amja"; about August the Bornu generals fought him at Lekarawa.

region.text: Bornu, which Rabih entered in summer 1893 and ruled from 2 October 1893 (the Cliopatria shape alive in 1893)

ledger.note: 2 October 1893: Rabih takes Kukawa and rules Bornu. "Upon reaching Kukawa, Rabih showed little mercy"; "The beginning of Rabih's rule over Bornu would later be dated to 2 October." The Bornu dossier keeps the contest to February/March 1894.

region.text: Bornu, which Rabih entered in summer 1893 and ruled from 2 October 1893 (the Cliopatria shape alive in 1893)

ledger.note: 2 October 1893: Bornu passes to Rabih. His rule over Bornu is dated 2 October; "Rabih conquered the Kanem-Bornu Empire".
c. 1894: Rabih moves his capital from Kukawa to Dikwa. The page says he "decided to transfer his capital to Dikwa" and gives no year.

region.text: Bagirmi, whose capital Massenya Rabih burnt in 1893

ledger.note: 1897: Bagirmi accepts a French protectorate by treaty, ending Rabih's hold on it; the French and Bagirmi forces killed him in 1900.

ledger.note: 22 April 1900: the battle of Kousséri. "The final showdown between Rabih and the French took place on April 22, 1900"; Rabih was shot while fleeing across the Chari; the French victory "ensured French control over most of Chad".

wars.outcome: The French column of Bretonnet was massacred at Togbao (July 1899); Lamy attacked Rabih's fortification at Lakhta near Kousséri on 22 April 1900 and Rabih was killed; Fadlallah was killed at Gujba on 23 August 1901.
wars.note: The French forces numbered 700 troops plus 600 riflemen and 200 cavalry of the Bagirmians; Major Lamy was killed.

notes:
State of Rabih az-Zubayr (the Zubat al-Kubar army state, Dar al-Kuti to Bornu), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. The slug is the one af-03-a and the Bornu dossier already use as counterpart. Pages: Rabih az-Zubayr, Battle of Kousséri, Bagirmi Sultanate.

Start: 1890 (the page's first place), not 1879, when the officers elected Rabih emir and the page gives no land; 1879-1891 are drawn only from 1890. Conflicts: Massenya taken 1892 (Rabih page) versus 1893 (Bagirmi page); Bornu contest end 2 October 1893 (here) versus February/March 1894 and a 1894 loss in the Bornu dossier; Rabih's end 1900 (death) versus the state's end with Fadlallah 1901. The Kousséri page does not name Dikwa as the capital (it mentions Dikoa where Rabih met de Béhagle); the Rabih page says he transferred the capital to Dikwa (no year).

Not on any page: the extent of Rabih's land; Dar Runga; where the Kotoko principalities lay (a disc at N'Djamena stands for them); the partition of 1902 (France, Britain, Germany). Gazetteer names needed: Dikwa, Kukawa, Dar al-Kuti (region), Dar Runga (region), Gujba, Lakhta, Amja, Massenya, Karnak Logone.
Counterparts: kotoko-city-states (Kousseri, Ngulfai, Logone; no dossier), dar-al-kuti, wadai-empire, empire-of-kanem, bagirmi-sultanate (this batch), french-africa.
